meta.title: How we work · delv.
meta.description: How a delv. engagement runs, where to start for a startup, a scale-up or an enterprise, and the six tests every deliverable has to pass before it leaves us.

blocks.name: Hero
blocks.heading: Priced before we start. Useful after we leave.
blocks.sub: We work inside your team rather than presenting to it. You see the deliverables and the price before you commit to anything, and what we hand over has to keep working once we have gone.

rows.heading: Discover
rows.body: We spend the first conversations on the problem you are solving, how you are solving it, and what your market is currently demanding of you. No proposal until we understand all three.

rows.heading: Brief
rows.body: We come back with a set of deliverables and indicative pricing, tied to your most urgent need without ignoring the medium term. You will know what you are buying and what it costs before you commit.

rows.heading: Investigate
rows.body: We meet stakeholders across commercial, marketing, product, data and clinical. We ask the awkward questions, find the gaps and the lever points, and zoom out to check where the market is heading.

rows.heading: Deliver
rows.body: Models, scenarios, real-world value, research and science communications strategy where relevant. Then the link to what happens next, because a value story that is not maintained ages quickly.

figure.label: Working session with a client team. Around a table or a screen, mid-discussion. Should read as an extension of their team, not a consultant presenting.

blocks.name: Where to start, where it goes next

groups.heading: Where to start
groups.lede: One entry point per audience, each a fixed fee agreed before we start. Every one of them ends with something you own whether or not you carry on with us.

items.heading: Value Audit
items.body: Where your claims stand, what your data can support, and a ranked list of what to fix first.

items.heading: Value Model Build
items.meta: Fixed fee · six to eight weeks
items.body: One defensible number built from your live deployment data, with the assumptions log and the business case template that carries it.

items.heading: Claims and Evidence Review
items.meta: Fixed fee · four to six weeks
items.body: Every claim you make in market, reconciled against its evidence, with a ranked remediation and retirement list.

groups.heading: Where it goes next
groups.lede: What most engagements become once the first piece has told us what is needed.

items.heading: Project
items.body: A defined build: a claims and evidence library, an ROI calculator or calculator estate, a business case pack, an investor evidence narrative.

items.heading: Embedded
items.body: We act as your value lead while you are too small to hire one. Useful through a raise, a tender cycle or a first outcomes-based contract.

blocks.name: Six tests
blocks.heading: Six tests for anything we hand over
paragraphs: Work that stops being useful the month after we invoice it was not worth buying. Every deliverable passes the same six tests before it leaves us.
items: Impactful: it changes a decision someone is about to make
Relevant: it speaks to your market, not to consultancy in general
Demonstrable: the evidence behind it can be produced on request
Quantifiable: there is a number, with a stated basis
Usable: your team can pick it up without us in the room
Marketable: it can go in front of customers and hold up

items.question: Why “delv.”?
items.answer: It is short for delivering value, and for delving deep enough into a business to find value worth shouting about.

items.question: Can we trust you to speak to our customers directly?
items.answer: Yes, and we have done it with organisations around the world. We are explicit about who we are, what we are asking and why, and we work to your rules on how your customers are approached. We turn up as part of your team, and your customers are told exactly that.

items.question: We already have a value-based agreement in place. Does that change things?
items.answer: It raises the stakes. Value-based agreements tie revenue to demonstrable health economic or operational outcomes, so evidence becomes a contractual obligation. That puts the contract and the revenue at risk. The position is usually recoverable if you start early enough.

items.question: Who do you usually work with?
items.answer: Companies of all sizes, but most often startups and scale-ups evidencing their value in order to sell, raise or exit. Investors use us too: a Value Audit to screen a company before backing it, or to find the readiness gaps in one already in the portfolio. Most of that work is aimed at the NHS, and we build for health systems outside the UK where the buyer, the budget and the evidence bar are all different.

items.question: How quickly can you start?
items.answer: Tell us your deadline in the first email. A Value Audit can usually begin within a fortnight; larger projects depend on the stakeholders we need access to.

items.question: What does it cost?
items.answer: Fixed fees for defined deliverables, or a day rate for advisory and embedded work, with specialist input such as health economics priced separately and transparently. You get pricing in the brief, before you commit.

blocks.name: Closing call to action
blocks.heading: Tell us what is stuck.
blocks.body: A first call costs nothing and usually clarifies the problem, whoever ends up solving it.
